intro: Before you spans Çobandede Bridge, in Erzurum province, built in the 14th century. This seven-arched Ilkhanid bridge crosses the Aras, and its ashlar work and pointed arches make it the most imposing medieval bridge in eastern Anatolia.
history: The seven-arched bridge over the Aras was built in the fourteenth century in the name of the Ilkhanid emir Çoban Noyan. Look at its ashlar work, its pointed arches and its flanking cutwaters: together they make it the most imposing medieval bridge in eastern Anatolia. For centuries, the Erzurum–Kars road ran across it.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the seven arches, the cutwaters, the ashlar parapet and the inscription.
facts: Did you know? The arches shrink from the middle outwards, a plan that both spreads the load and lets flood water through more easily. For its ashlar work, this seven-arched Ilkhanid bridge is the most imposing medieval bridge in eastern Anatolia.
outro: This brings our tour of Çobandede Bridge to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for walking with us, and enjoy your visit.
